name: freesave-read-flipped
symbols_from_why: gFreeSaveHookLatch and gFreeSaveOffsets are fork-only symbols.

probes.why: THE CLAIM. Sectors 0 and 4 are the only two whose SIZE changes, their checksums are recomputed over the new length, and one bad sector costs the whole slot. SAVE_STATUS_CORRUPT == 2.
BELOW THE CUT (0x234, unmoved). Predicted to survive: sector 1 keeps its size, so it keeps passing its checksum and is copied.

ABOVE THE CUT. This build's flags[] moved 156 bytes down, so the FLAG_SYS_POKEDEX_GET byte is now at 4564+268 = 4832. Predicted to be misread — it will read whatever lived 156 bytes earlier in the old layout.
THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME FACT: 4988, where that byte lived in the writing build. Predicted 2 — the data is still there, byte for byte; it is the FIELD that moved.
ABOVE THE CUT. vars[] moved 156 down: VAR_RECYCLE_GOODS is now at 4864+64 = 4928. Predicted misread.
5084, its old home. Predicted 0x5AA5 — exact, non-zero, and a value nothing else in the engine writes, which is what makes it a claim about THIS byte rather than about memory being non-empty.

THE TAIL. This build's dexCaught is at 12677, still past 11904 and so still in sector 4 — the sector whose size changed from 3664 to 1248. Predicted 0: a sector that fails its checksum is SKIPPED, not repaired.

13849, the writing build's dexCaught. Predicted 0 as well, and for a DIFFERENT reason than dex_caught0 — not because the field moved but because the whole sector was never copied. Two zeros with two causes; the pair is what separates 'moved' from 'gone'.
SECTOR 0, SaveBlock2. Its size changed 3884 to 2544, so predicted 0.
OBSERVATION. Where a corrupt-but-partially-loadable save actually leaves the player is the thing this round most wants a picture of.

assert.why: THE CLAIM, AND THE ONLY STRONG ASSERTION THIS ARM CAN CARRY. SAVE_STATUS_CORRUPT == 2, exact and non-zero. Everything else here is a compare against zero -- doc 55 §9.4's weak class -- and it is weak by NECESSITY rather than by neglect: the finding is that the values are gone, and gone has only one representation. What makes the zeros mean something is the control arm reading 1, 17, 2, 0x5AA5, 255 and 7 out of the SAME FILE. Doc 61 §4's pair rule: the proof is the pair of runs, not the spec that passes.
SUPPORTING, weak class (compare against zero). Was 1 in the control, on the identical file.
SUPPORTING, weak class (compare against zero). Was 17 in the control. Below the cut and copied by CopySaveSlotData -- and then wiped anyway.
SUPPORTING, weak class (compare against zero). Was 2 in the control. The bytes are gone from RAM, not merely displaced.
SUPPORTING, weak class (compare against zero). Was 0x5AA5 in the control.
SUPPORTING, weak class (compare against zero). Was 255 in the control.
SUPPORTING, weak class (compare against zero). Was 7 in the control.
CONTROL. A cold CPU start named by symbol -- and it is the exact function whose body contains the Sav2_ClearSetDefault() call this arm is about.
